name: Major cyber incidents
value: France blames IRGC for destructive fridge hacks
summary: France blamed an IRGC unit on 9 Nov for attacks on refrigeration in about 700 stores that caused at least 15 fires
state: On 9 Nov French agencies attributed the 11–12 Oct attacks on refrigeration controllers in about 700 stores, which caused at least 15 fires, to Shahid Kaveh, an IRGC cyber unit, naming three commanders (The Record; The National). France summoned Iran's ambassador and sought EU sanctions on 10 Nov. Microsoft's 10 Nov updates fixed an Outlook flaw already exploited in attacks (CyberScoop). A destructive state-attributed attack keeps the Alert.
for_you: Organisations running internet-connected building, refrigeration or industrial controls are most exposed; NCSC and CISA publish guidance on securing operational technology. Applying Microsoft's November updates closes the exploited Outlook flaw.
rubric_hit: Destructive state-attributed attack (IRGC unit, ~700 stores, 15+ fires; attributed 9 Nov) = Alert

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
